Keywords: Mounted archery bowstrings arrows and horses
RagShortTexts: Mounted archery depends on bows, practice and horses.
Damp, fatigue and scarce arrows limit continued action.

Variants.Content: Mongol mounted archery combines riding, shooting and unit movement. Glue joints, strings, arrows and horses need care. Distance and contact with companions matter; fatigue, damp and exhausted arrows force changes and replenishment.
An archer watches mount and formation as well as target. Replenishment requires contact with support; riding fastest may outrun one’s own arrows and remounts.
Mounted archers cost arrows, strings, forage and training. Forced pursuit reduces next-day usable strength below nominal numbers.
Arrow makers and bow repairers need materials and time, while supporting households tend spare horses. Neglected contributors mean shortages of arrows and remounts.
